**Prepared inline for parent persistence only.** No file was written, no checklist item was marked complete, and no sibling synthesis content was read.

**Destination:** `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/fix-flaky-parallel-thread-test/.dev/tasks/to-do/TASK-RESEARCH-sub-orchestrator-mode-20261108-181115/synthesis/synth-06-questions-evidence.md`

## 9. Open Questions

The questions below distinguish unresolved design decisions, unverified execution, and evidence limitations. They do not reopen facts already established elsewhere in the research package.

**Evidence references:** R01–R08 and W01–W04 identify the exact research files listed in Section 10. Each includes its complete returned JSON companion. G01–G54 and S01–S38 identify the compiled gaps and stale-documentation families in the gaps log. References to research sections include the corresponding full returned investigation, not just its Markdown index.

**Scope boundary:** This is a read-only decision investigation. Every suggested live Orca or harness verification below requires separate authorization and is **out of scope here**. Suggested resolutions are evidence requirements or decisions, not an implementation sequence.

### Source-established facts that are not open questions

| Reference | Established finding and remaining boundary |
|---|---|
| C1 — corrected guard scope | R04’s B1/B2 addendum, carried through R05 and R07, limits the relevant Orca classifier claim to positively bound sessions and recognized literal `orca` forms. It does not establish coverage of every executable spelling or successful bypass. Required worker enumeration, transcript and prompt-wait probes are not all listed exceptions. Launch authority, upward messaging and supervision-probe compatibility remain separate decisions. |
| C2 — current Orca mechanics | R03 establishes native local helper routing to a live same-Run creator Dispatch, with Run fallback and selected-mail handback after creator settlement. It also establishes the current depth classifications, independent coordinator authority on Task creation, and validated workspace lineage. These are source findings, not successful live nesting or complete recovery proof. Earlier slice-local “routing unknown” or “current six routes untraced” statements do not override them. |
| C3 — documented incoming-message hooks | W01 establishes a documented affirmative answer to #339’s inbound-hook question: `UserPromptSubmit` includes another session’s message to the main conversation and can block it. Documented default delivery compares permission classes, not exact mode-name equality. Deployment coverage, trusted sender metadata, timeout behavior and safe authorization remain unresolved. External context: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#userpromptsubmit and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#control-inbound-messages . |
| C4 — existing authority | R01 and R06 establish the current worker-session prohibition, person-opened coordinator definition, explicit unattended-mode selection, person-only Rulings, ordinary PR-session policy and Task-specific local-commit grants. Their status is not unknown merely because another research slice did not inspect the decision records. Any extension is a new decision; existing restrictions continue to apply. |
| C5 — public versus installed defaults | W04 distinguishes the inspected installed default and stored value of one from newer public default-four and migration statements. Public release behavior is not evidence of the installed runtime’s effective setting or current shutdown guarantees. External context: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348 . |
| C6 — controlling quantitative correction | W02’s correction addendum governs its immutable return: approximately two detected bugs per Devin-authored PR reviewed by Devin Review; approximately 58% of **detected bugs** classified severe; approximately eightfold usage growth only in Cognition’s **largest enterprises segment**, with usage metric and absolute baseline unspecified. These are operational observations, not a hierarchy-versus-flat benchmark or a local performance forecast. External context: https://cognition.com/blog/multi-agents-working . |
| C7 — approved inventory scope | R07’s later approval limits the active change-impact inventory to current sources, tests and distributed copies. Its older partial-status text does not make that approved inventory incomplete. The historical unread residual remains excluded, unverified background, as recorded below. |

### Open Questions table

All proposed capabilities and unproved behavior in this table remain **[UNVERIFIED]** unless the question is explicitly an unresolved policy choice.

| # | Question | Impact (what it blocks) | Suggested Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q01 | What precise role would “a coordinator under another orchestrator” denote, and how would an agent-launched nonworker qualify for it? **R01, R08; G02/G51; W04.** | A consistent interpretation of PR #449 and a defensible choice between supervised helpers, independent peers and a handoff-owner role. | Require an explicit role definition covering eligibility, upper owner, permitted planning, child ownership and reporting. Record the PR #449/WC-13 conflict as a defect with the existing INF-027 deferral, not as implicit permission. |
| Q02 | What complete upward relationship would an O4 launched owner have, and how would independent O2 peers divide work without acquiring control of one another’s Tasks? **R01–R03, R05–R08; G19/G33/G51.** | Treating an ordinary launch or peer exchange as a supervised assignment with progress, questions, completion and recovery. | Require a written ownership and reporting contract covering correlation, acknowledgments, durable results, admission, failure and closure. Keep launch receipts distinct from completion. |
| Q03 | Is the proposed entry point a coordinator-only Orca-calling command, a session role outside commands, or an internal-helper wrapper? **R01/R07/R08; G35.** | Command boundaries, unattended-mode behavior, eligibility and never-as-worker treatment—even without a sub mode. | Require an explicit architectural decision addressing the no-Orca-command rule, the coordinator-only claim-launch precedent, D1 and the applicable eligibility lists. |
| Q04 | What would an autonomous composite brief authorize, including child planning, helper count, write scope, question allowance and result obligations? **R01/R06/R08; G03.** | D5 reconsideration and bounded O3 delegation. | Require an approved brief definition with explicit limits and completion/admission responsibilities. Do not substitute prewritten command chains for discretionary dispatch authority. |
| Q05 | Is there a qualifying real run with a split knowable only during execution and a measured, material extra coordinator round trip? **R06; G10; W02/W04.** | Establishing D5’s measured-need condition or claiming demonstrated local value. | Locate a record identifying the original Task, newly discovered split, why it was not reasonably knowable beforehand, follow-up Task and added coordination time. Preserve the bounded-search qualification if no record is available. |
| Q06 | Was omission of the recommendation’s mailbox prerequisite from the applied D5 short record intentional or a summarization loss? **R06 §2; G11.** | An unambiguous future reconsideration decision. | Require an authoritative disposition of the textual difference. Neither assume a waiver nor infer that source routing alone satisfies operational verification. |
| Q07 | What constitutes a middle session’s own semantic progress, separately from child activity, repeated messages and monitoring traffic? **R02; G04; W02.** | Reliable supervision of the middle session and meaningful aggregate progress reporting. | Require explicit own-work and subtree-progress semantics with attributable evidence and handling of an idle or blocked parent with active children. |
| Q08 | How do child succeeded, usable-partial, failed, blocked and dropped outcomes determine aggregate status and admission? **R01/R02/R08; G04.** | Trustworthy aggregate completion, dependency release and integration. | Require a recursive outcome/admission contract preserving each required child’s evidence, exclusions and unresolved effects, with a named admission owner. |
| Q09 | Who handles mixed parent/helper FIFO batches, and how do Delivery acknowledgments differ from applied/queued/refused acknowledgments across both edges? **R02/R03; G05; W02.** | Avoiding lost instructions, premature acknowledgment and false claims that a child applied an upper-level decision. | Require one accountable handling/acknowledgment owner per mailbox and a mixed-batch acceptance record. **Live nested delivery/ack verification is out of scope here.** |
| Q10 | Who continues servicing and monitoring children when their parent asks upstream, is blocked, fenced, exhausted, exits or is replaced? **R02/R03; G06.** | Preventing unattended descendants and overlapping supervisors. | Require an explicit service/takeover policy and ownership-transfer evidence, including retained pending questions and reports. **Live failure/replacement verification is out of scope here.** |
| Q11 | How are helper count, total attempts, failed starts, restart limits, probes, time and resource budgets accounted for across the whole lineage? **R01/R02/R06; G07; W02/W04.** | Bounded autonomy and prevention of multiplicative retries or independently reset allowances. | Require a lineage-wide budget definition that survives replacement and distinguishes depth, concurrency, retries and total resource use. |
| Q12 | Who may cancel, settle, release or clean up a subtree, and what establishes descendant quiescence and orphan disposition? **R01/R02/R08; G07; W02/W04.** | Safe recovery and destructive cleanup. | Require one accountable authority per operation, positive settlement/quiescence evidence and an explicit treatment of uncertain or preserved descendants. Do not treat parent termination as subtree settlement. |
| Q13 | How would a halted implementation freeze propagate to all relevant descendant writers and survive parent replacement? **R01/R06/R08; G07/G34.** | Safe resumption, shared Git operations and protection of halted evidence. | Require explicit freeze scope, permitted report-only behavior, human hand-back provenance and preservation of the actual halted worktree, plan and baseline. |
| Q14 | How would L5 escalation and person-only decisions reach the actual person through an unattended middle layer? **R01/R02/R06; G08; W02.** | Preserving human authority and bounded escalation rather than merely reporting to another agent. | Require a relay contract with origin, acknowledgment, deadline, responsible owner and final human visibility. |
| Q15 | What, if anything, could be delegated about commit grants, PR ownership, outward actions, merges or removal without widening the person’s instruction? **R01/R06/R08; G33/G34; W03.** | Any claim of transitive human authorization or inherited publishing/cleanup authority. | Require a separate authority decision preserving Task-specific grant provenance and termination. A parent credential or role name must not be accepted as a new user instruction or Ruling. |
| Q16 | Can the existing compact worker handoff preserve a supervisor’s child roster, budgets, Deliveries, applied decisions, admissions, ownership and uncertain effects? **R02; G09; W02.** | Reliable middle-session recovery without forgetting live work or redoing completed steps. | Require a supervisor-checkpoint sufficiency assessment against those fields; retain explicit omissions until evidenced. |
| Q17 | Does the inspected native local helper path execute correctly through startup, question/reply, completion, mixed mail, fencing, early parent settlement and recovery? **R03; G12; W02/W04.** | Calling O3 operationally verified rather than source-supported. | Require a separately authorized, version-recorded lifecycle acceptance record covering each scenario. **A live Orca run is out of scope here.** |
| Q18 | What are the complete remote/federated helper authority, depth, separate-Run reporting and recovery guarantees on each host? **R03; G13; W04.** | Extending local conclusions to remote execution or assuming desktop settings govern remote workers. | Require host-specific source/guide evidence and separately authorized end-to-end validation, including remote configuration ownership. **Live federation runs are out of scope here.** |
| Q19 | What maximum is effectively loaded by the running Orca runtime, what storage backs it, and how do reload and profile propagation behave? **R03; G14; W04.** | Treating stored data as active policy or bounding the effect of a change. | Require a complete settings/getter trace and, if still needed, separately authorized observation of effective values and reload. **Live setting changes are out of scope here.** |
| Q20 | Is lowering the maximum safe while deeper workers, pending questions or unsettled effects remain? **R03; G15.** | A defensible rollback or reversibility claim. | Require an authorized rollback acceptance record covering existing helpers, new starts, questions, settlement and recovery. **Live lowering is out of scope here.** |
| Q21 | What remains outside the inspected public CLI/schema evidence concerning internal overrides and settings scope? **R03; G16; W04.** | Universal “no override anywhere” or “all profiles on the machine change” claims. | Preserve the bounded finding and require further authoritative interface/storage evidence only if the decision depends on a broader claim. Do not invent a per-Run control. |
| Q22 | What identities and refusal receipts occur for the particular live sessions and entry points being evaluated? **R03; G17.** | Promoting source-level depth classification into observed refusal or successful execution. | Require a separately authorized identity/refusal record for the relevant build and caller context. **Live dispatch or alternate-launch probes are out of scope here.** |
| Q23 | Does the separately inspected development checkout exactly match the installed backend as a whole? **R02/R03; G20.** | Claims of whole-build equivalence based on corroborated individual routing paths. | Require revision/build provenance or a bounded equivalence comparison. Do not reopen installed-source routing merely because complete build equivalence is unproved. |
| Q24 | Which provider, adapter, permission, concurrency and nested-background lifecycle limits apply to the installed internal-subagent harness? **R03; G18; W01/W02/W04.** | A universal assertion that internal helpers are unlimited or that current public nesting defaults apply locally. | Require installed capability/version and relevant adapter evidence. Any necessary live harness check is **out of scope here**. |
| Q25 | How does the actual default mailbox wait wake when types are not explicitly supplied? **R02; G23.** | Reliable wait design and detection assumptions. | Require authoritative current behavior evidence or separately authorized observation. **A live consuming wait is out of scope here.** |
| Q26 | What caused the historical missed answers, and does the current response detect non-application reliably? **R02; G23.** | A confirmed diagnosis or claim that the answer-delivery problem is fixed. | Require incident evidence separating delivery, wake, read, application and acknowledgment. **Live reproduction is out of scope here.** |
| Q27 | Which attention categories are exposed, and what delay precedes permission-prompt or context-exhaustion detection? **R02; G23.** | Measured detection bounds and correct treatment of unknown versus evaluated-null observations. | Require category and timing evidence for the actual build. **Live prompt/attention verification is out of scope here.** |
| Q28 | What happens to typed input during an active tool call? **R02; G23.** | Any expansion beyond the existing positively idle input boundary. | Require separately authorized runtime evidence before relying on such behavior. **Live typing experiments are out of scope here.** |
| Q29 | What happens with simultaneous consumers of one mailbox in the running build? **R02/R03; G05/G23.** | Safe multiple-consumer assumptions and replacement handling. | Require an explicit concurrency/consumer-generation acceptance record. **Live mailbox consumption and acknowledgment are out of scope here.** |
| Q30 | How reliably do agents execute the existing sweep, progress-token, acknowledgment, chain, handoff and timing procedures? **R01/R02/R05/R06/R08; G01.** | Universal compliance or automatic-monitoring claims based on phrase tests. | Require observed behavioral evidence for the relevant procedure and scope. **Live worker checks are out of scope here.** |
| Q31 | Have all eight reported #431 incident families been eliminated, and are claimed detection/escalation bounds actually met? **R02/R08; G25.** | Treating merged procedural #434 as demonstrated incident resolution. | Require incident-specific acceptance evidence and measured timing. **Live reproduction or supervised test runs are out of scope here.** |
| Q32 | Which proposed C10–C14 monitor, hook, dashboard, context-telemetry and persistent-budget mechanisms have actually been delivered elsewhere? **R02; G26.** | Claims of deterministic monitoring or durable budget machinery. | Require a bounded implementation/deployment inventory. Keep future proposals distinct from current procedures and from stale documentation. |
| Q33 | What writes and persists workspace lineage, beyond the inspected schema, projection and host/instance validation? **R03; G22.** | A complete backing-storage or persistence-recovery claim. | Require a targeted persistence trace if that property is material to the selected option; retain the existing validity findings. |
| Q34 | What complete backend validation, if any, applies to referenced report files and artifacts? **R02; G24.** | Assuming settlement or a receipt means the returned evidence was read and validated. | Require a complete backend trace before assigning that guarantee. Retain explicit supervisor-side report reading and admission. |
| Q35 | What trusted binding would identify role, authorized parent, child scope and permitted reporting destination? **R01/R04/R07/R08; G27/G51/G52.** | Role-aware authorization and any narrow exception for a middle session. | Require an authority model and binding evidence covering launch, upward communication and required supervision separately. Do not assume names, unbound state or a classifier mismatch supply permission. |
| Q36 | What authoritative Orca preamble and parent/session identity, if any, reaches actual hook events and nested subagent events? **R04; G28; W01/W04.** | U7 resolution and reliance on hand-written event fixtures as runtime identity evidence. | Require actual envelope/provenance evidence for the relevant paths. **Live worker/subagent event capture is out of scope here.** |
| Q37 | What is the actual resolution of U28’s Orca-hooks/L2 pre-push installation question? **R04; G29; W04.** | Treating installation capability as established, or conflating it with preamble visibility. | Require the specific installation/runtime evidence for U28 independently of U7. |
| Q38 | How do concurrent whole-input hook rewrites, working-directory behavior and Linux job attribution behave in practice? **R04; G30.** | Reliable rewritten-input enforcement and process attribution. | Require ordering and execution-context evidence, including declared detachment/daemonization limits. **Live rewrite/job experiments are out of scope here.** |
| Q39 | Is the child governed before its first consequential tool call, with effective enforcement in its own eventual environment? **R04/R05; G31.** | Treating claim-process preflight as proof of child enforcement. | Require a complete claim-to-binding/first-tool acceptance record. **A live claim launch is out of scope here.** |
| Q40 | Which source, plugin, development, packaged and installed copies are current and equivalent for the exact deployment being evaluated? **R04/R05/R07/R08; G32.** | Universal freshness, parity or distribution-success claims. | Require a bounded copy/provenance record and separately authorized execution evidence where necessary. Do not equate development sync, plugin packaging and global installation. No sync/build/install/test run is authorized here. |
| Q41 | Does D3’s ordinary-session-per-PR placement occur automatically and consistently in practice? **R05; G36.** | Treating a recorded placement policy as an implemented launcher guarantee. | Require implementation or observed-placement evidence without moving PR submission into supervised workers. **Live session placement checks are out of scope here.** |
| Q42 | Do PM, agent and issue helpers follow their stated roles, outputs and tier assignments, and is PM’s claimed startup behavior registered? **R05; G37.** | Reusing those instructions as proven execution or coordinator precedents. | Require registration/resolution evidence and bounded behavior records. **Live helper/model execution is out of scope here.** |
| Q43 | Are issue-watch’s assumed launch-operation fields, unknown-operation error and lost-response handling valid for the installed Orca interface? **R05; G38.** | Reliable launch deduplication and recovery from uncertain receipts. | Require an authoritative interface contract and separately authorized compatibility evidence. **Live launch/lost-response experiments are out of scope here.** |
| Q44 | What isolation and effect boundaries actually constrain subprocess launchers? **R05; G39; W04.** | Treating environment isolation, bypass flags or a depth ceiling as a filesystem, permission or spending sandbox. | Require explicit containment evidence and a threat-model statement before using these launchers as an authority precedent. |
| Q45 | How does native messaging represent and verify the sender’s permission class? **R08; G40; W01.** | Fully closing #339’s first transport question. | Require an authoritative interface/implementation account of class identification and validation. Do not invent a per-send assertion or infer identity from message text. |
| Q46 | What were the sender mode, effective receiving settings and runtime behavior in #339’s historical held-message incident? **W01; G40.** | A proven incident diagnosis or assertion that a particular launch configuration caused it. | Require historical configuration/receipt evidence; otherwise preserve it as an unreproduced report. Any reproduction is **out of scope here**. |
| Q47 | Which documented messaging features and incoming-hook routes apply to the installed harness across active, idle, remote and nested contexts? **W01/W02; G40.** | A deployed feature or universal interception guarantee. | Require installed version/capability and route-specific evidence. The documented main-conversation hook answer remains affirmative. **Live delivery/event tests are out of scope here.** |
| Q48 | What authenticated sender and parent metadata can a receiver validate, and is genuinely parent-specific acceptance available? **W01/W03; G27/G40/G42.** | Narrow acceptance of an authorized parent rather than broad inbound trust. | Require a trusted-origin/presentation contract that does not confuse receiving-session fields or text assertions with sender identity. |
| Q49 | Does deployed incoming validation fail closed on timeout, error and ordering failures? **W01; G40.** | A dependable security boundary rather than a hook that merely can block normally. | Require installation, timeout/error and ordering evidence for the selected hook mechanism. **Live failure-injection verification is out of scope here.** |
| Q50 | Does the actual incoming prompt envelope keep peer text distinct from genuine human plan approval and other person-only decisions? **W01; G08/G34/G40.** | Preventing agent messages from being treated as human consent. | Require origin-separation evidence for the approval parser and incoming-message path. No successful laundering is established. **Live security experiments are out of scope here.** |
| Q51 | What complete typed-message or validated-file protocol would enforce IDs, resource scope, freshness, inert free text, acknowledgments and result admission? **R08; G41; W01/W03.** | Treating plain-text envelopes or valid file syntax as authorization and safe completion. | Require a complete protocol and trusted-producer/validation boundary, including a deliberate mapping to existing transport semantics. |
| Q52 | Which grant policy could authorize restricted requests or actions, including downward attenuation, without silently delegating current human-only authority? **R08; G34/G42; W03.** | The proposed grant layer and hierarchy’s downward authority. | Require a policy decision distinguishing request permission from execution authority, issuer/verifier trust, resource/action scope and destructive-action preconditions. |
| Q53 | What are the existing Dispatch capability’s semantics, attenuation and lifecycle, and is it suitable for the proposed grants? **R08; G43; W03.** | Choosing reuse versus a separate credential mechanism. | Require a complete capability trace before claiming it is absent, equivalent or insufficient. |
| Q54 | Where would complete trusted authorization occur before every relevant effect, given the inspected hooks’ boundaries? **R04; G42/G52; W03/W04.** | A non-bypassable enforcement claim or token-based security assurance. | Require an explicit effect/enforcement map and threat model. Credential integrity alone must not stand in for interception, trusted context or authorization. |
| Q55 | How would one-use grants be consumed atomically across concurrent receivers, retries and duplicate delivery? **W03; G42.** | Replay prevention. | Require a consumption-state and duplicate/idempotency contract with explicit scope and failure handling. A nonce field alone is not sufficient evidence. |
| Q56 | What trusted clock, expiry, key/discharge or attestation policy, revocation distribution and outage/freshness rules would apply? **W03; G42.** | Effective expiry and revocation, especially offline or after subtree cancellation. | Require a credential-lifecycle policy distinguishing local chain verification, fresh proof acquisition, revocation knowledge and retained broader credentials. |
| Q57 | Which maintained Python/Node implementation and feature set fits the deployment, and what is the separately requested adversarial selection result? **R08; G42; W03.** | Closing #339’s third question or adopting a dependency. | Require supported-version, security-maintenance, compatibility and feature evidence, including third-party support; obtain the separately authorized comparison decision. A research preference is not its winner. |
| Q58 | What workload and observed evidence would validate the stated 10–20-session target? **R08; G44; W02.** | A capacity or scalability claim. | Require local workload, supervision and outcome evidence rather than vendor research metrics or synthetic dashboard scale. |
| Q59 | How would persistent orchestrator registration and routing obligations cover ordinary sessions, later-opened sessions and multiple owners? **R08; G44.** | #339’s permanent-role/all-session objective. | Require a role/registry ownership contract with eligibility and explicit exceptions; do not substitute Dispatch identity for an all-session registry. |
| Q60 | What is the intended configurable historical-session sweep, including the six-hour window and its relationship to live worker supervision? **R08; G44.** | Treating #339’s proposed sweep interface as already supplied by current liveness rules. | Require explicit scope and acceptance criteria separating recent-session inventory from ongoing supervision. |
| Q61 | What would keep attention requests visible until satisfied and provide the proposed periodic static report without falsely equating acknowledgment with resolution? **R08; G44.** | Persistent attention and reporting requirements. | Require an evidence-backed display/closure contract, reporting cadence and an explicit disposition of response-style conflicts. |
| Q62 | What management server, endpoint and information/authority boundary does #339 intend? **R08; G44.** | Any server-relay integration or ownership claim. | Require an identified service contract and data/control boundary. |
| Q63 | What proves all required commits are pushed, work is admitted, protected evidence is retained and relevant sessions are closed before cleanup? **R08; G44; W01/W03/W04.** | Safe session/worktree/branch closure. | Require explicit predicates and an accountable checker, preserving frozen-state, unread-report, unfinished-ledger, merge and human-instruction protections. Idle notices and authenticated close requests are not substitutes. |
| Q64 | How should conflicting proposals for universal automation, disposable artifacts, worktree-per-prompt placement, response-table replacement and supervised fan-out be dispositioned? **R08; G50.** | Consistent v1 and hierarchy acceptance criteria. | Require explicit requirement/policy dispositions. Do not silently adopt proposals that conflict with current protections or imply an exception from a role label. |
| Q65 | How will release ownership and numbering distinguish v1 supervision, #423 knowledge sharing and later hierarchy/security work? **R08; G45.** | Administrative acceptance and release claims. | Record a release-scope decision. The semantic distinction is already established; only the administrative allocation remains open. |
| Q66 | What verified remote implementation, version, schema, tests and live collection contract back #409? **R08; G46.** | Treating the observer proposal or synthetic data as a deployed API, capacity proof or controller. | Require actual source/provenance evidence in a separately scoped investigation. Preserve its observer-only boundary. |
| Q67 | What evidence establishes #446’s lock/environment experiments and the remaining #326 Git, submodule and per-task commit work? **R08; G47.** | Assuming these independent follow-ups are implemented or provide new middle-layer Git authority. | Require issue-specific evidence and current acceptance records; keep them separate from hierarchy and preserve the current lock/freeze/ownership restrictions. |
| Q68 | Where is P2 live acceptance, distinct from the merged static conversion? **R06/R08; G48.** | Calling the rollout live-accepted or later phases ready. | Require the applicable live phase/acceptance record; retain the bounded “not found” qualification rather than claiming global absence. |
| Q69 | What local evidence establishes incremental hierarchy benefit, security adequacy or reliable recovery beyond the inspected external mechanisms and differently scoped benchmarks? **G49; W02/W03/W04.** | A numerical speedup/cost/reliability promise, a “trustless” security claim or a measured delivery estimate. | Require relevant local comparison and threat-model evidence. Preserve corrected denominators and source limitations; neither vendor adoption figures nor CaMeL’s task-completion result substitutes for local proof. |
| Q70 | What would a future Orca upgrade/migration actually do to this profile and each execution host? **W04.** | Assuming an intentional older value of one survives unchanged or public default four is already active. | Require a separately authorized version/migration review tied to actual profile and host state. **Upgrades and setting mutations are out of scope here.** |
| Q71 | Which descendant-stop, preservation, uncertain-stop, interrupted-start and detached-process behaviors apply to this installation? **W04; G06/G07.** | Assuming a newer public shutdown announcement guarantees complete local subtree termination. | Require build-specific source evidence and a separately authorized shutdown/recovery acceptance record. **Live stop/cleanup experiments are out of scope here.** |

### Evidence limitations retained without inventing new product questions

These limitations remain visible but do not require reopening the approved current-source inventory or performing unrelated research before this decision report can be assembled.

| Reference | Limitation and disposition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| B01 — historical P0 observations | Raw historical worker transcripts were not independently replayed. The P0 reports remain documentary execution evidence; absence of forbidden calls is not a demonstrated rejection of attempted calls. Historical AC-0.7 completion remains distinct from current source verification and live nesting. | G21; R03 §6 and complete return; R06 phase-evidence tables. |
| B02 — excluded archival residual | The frozen historical inventory retains **867 unread matching lines across 274 paths**. These remain unread/unclassified background outside the user-approved current-source/tests/distributed-copy scope. Their existence is not a demand for another archival audit, nor evidence that current active-surface research is incomplete. | G53; R07 approval, ledger and both archival supplements. |
| B03 — historical notebook | The moved LangGraph notebook and incomplete historical extraction do not establish unobserved supervisor/context-adapter internals. Exclude those internals from conclusions; the inspected architectural descriptions remain usable as external context. | W02 source-access limitation and original gap 14. |
| B04 — macaroon paper extraction | The original PDF body was not fully readable with the research tools. Preserve the stated abstract/indexed-passages/implementation-documentation boundary; do not claim a complete original-paper read. | W03 method and original gap 7. |
| B05 — inaccessible public implementation | The inspected public Orca implementation URL returned 404 for an unknown reason. Do not infer privacy, implementation absence or verified source content from that result. | W04 negative searches and original gap 13. |
| B06 — exact public depth choice | The inspected public rationale supports a finite ceiling but does not explain why exactly four was chosen. That missing rationale is excluded as a basis for choosing a local limit; it is not a prerequisite to preserve today’s contract. | W04 original gap 6. |
| B07 — estimates and unexecuted checks | Reported issue estimates, historical test counts and inspected-but-unrun tests, sync, packaging and installation procedures are not new execution results. The source inventory and identified precedents do not certify deployment readiness. | R05/R07/R08; G32/G44/G47/G48. |

### Stale-documentation and interpretation dispositions

These entries surface all 38 compiled families without pretending their source-answered portions are still open questions. Historical records are retained, not rewritten into present permission.

| Compiled families | Disposition in this report | Residual question or limitation |
|---|---|---|
| S01 | Evaluate the final session-layer scoped D5 alternative, not the original command-owned-worker/command-rewrite proposal. | Q03/Q04/Q15. |
| S02 | A higher valid maximum is not removal of the depth fence. | Q19–Q22. |
| S03, S04 | “Spec not edited” and “none applied yet” are historical drafting status, not current D5 status. | No missing decision-status fact; Q06 concerns the actual remaining textual discrepancy. |
| S05 | D1–D5 and Git ownership are settled in the authoritative records. | Q15 concerns future delegation, not whether those decisions exist. |
| S06, S07 | The root-coordinator precondition and worker-session rule are present in the applied/current policy. | Q01/Q04 concern a new role or exception. |
| S08 | CR-01’s not-applied status is historical; placement/isolation provisions were applied. | Q12/Q63 concern future ownership and safe cleanup. |
| S09 | The earlier P0-smoke trigger is superseded by the two-part composite-brief/material-runtime-split trigger. | Q04/Q05. |
| S10 | Multiple prewritten command lines are supported; this does not establish autonomous child-dispatch authority. | Q04. |
| S11 | Old specification anchors must not be reused as current locations. | Citation-history limitation, not a missing architecture fact. |
| S12 | The older setup-run wording does not override the newer authorization-sensitive setup-skip default. | No setup action is authorized; any extension belongs to Q15. |
| S13 | The older never-as-worker inventory omitting issue does not replace the current contract/test inventory. | Q03 for a genuinely new entry point. |
| S14 | Historical PR-worker/opt-in proposals do not override current ordinary top-level PR-session policy. | Q41 concerns observed placement, not current policy. |
